extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and others filing correspondence or papers with the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for preparing, addressing, signing, identifying, and submitting correspondence and filings to the USPTO (including mail stop/marking requirements, signature formats, receipt/date rules, facsimile and electronic filing rules, certificates of mailing/transmission, and related procedural requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Address correspondence to appropriate Mail Stop/Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence in an application or a patent involved in an appeal or other proceeding should be addressed to the appropriate Mail Stop or Office specified by the USPTO (e.g., Office of General Counsel, Office of the Solicitor, Office of Public Records Assignment Recordation Services, Office of Enrollment and Discipline, Mail Stop Maintenance Fee, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text lists specific mail stops and addresses (e.g., Mail Stop 8, Office of the Solicitor, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450; Mail Stop Assignment Recordation Services; Mail Stop Maintenance Fee). Correspondence improperly addressed to a Post Office Box specified for particular offices may not be filed elsewhere in the USPTO and may be returned. For international-stage PCT correspondence, additionally mark 'Mail Stop PCT.' For reexamination/supplemental/ex parte/inter partes proceedings, mark 'Mail Stop Ex Parte Reexam', 'Mail Stop Inter Partes Reexam', or 'Mail Stop Supplemental Examination' as appropriate. For patent term extension under 35 U.S.C. 156/Hatch-Waxman, mark 'Mail Stop Hatch-Waxman PTE' and, when appropriate, mark to the attention of a particular individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business must be transacted in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: All business with the Patent and Trademark Office should be transacted in writing; personal attendance is unnecessary and action will be based exclusively on the written record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No attention will be paid to any alleged oral promise, stipulation, or understanding in relation to which there is disagreement or doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct business with decorum and courtesy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and their attorneys or agents are required to conduct business with the USPTO with decorum and courtesy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers presented in violation of this requirement will be submitted to the Director and will not be entered; a notice of non-entry will be provided. Complaints against examiners and other employees must be made in correspondence separate from other papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish types of correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence comprises (1) correspondence relating to services and facilities of the Office (general inquiries, requests for publications, orders for printed copies, assignments for recording, etc.) and (2) correspondence in and relating to a particular application or other proceeding in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See relevant subparts for filing/processing rules: national applications (subpart B), international applications (subpart C), ex parte reexaminations (subpart D), supplemental examination (subpart E), patent term extension (subpart F), inter partes reexaminations (subpart H), international design applications (subpart I), and PTAB parts 41 and 42.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a separate copy for each file
rubrics_metrics.description: A separate copy of every paper to be filed in a patent application, patent file, or other proceeding must be furnished for each file to which the paper pertains because each file must be complete in itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid filing duplicate copies of correspondence except where the Office requires duplicates. The Office may dispose of duplicate copies of correspondence in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate subjects must be on separate papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Each distinct subject, inquiry, or order must be contained in a separate paper to avoid confusion and delay in answering papers dealing with different subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects provided for on a single Office or WIPO form may be contained in a single paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handwritten signature requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each piece of correspondence that requires a person's signature must be an original handwritten signature personally signed in permanent dark ink or be a direct or indirect copy (e.g., photocopy or facsimile) of an original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design patent practitioners must indicate their design status by placing the word 'design' adjacent to their handwritten signature. If a copy is filed, the original should be retained as evidence of authenticity; the Office may require submission of the original if authenticity is questioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-signature format and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An S-signature is a signature inserted between forward slash marks (e.g., /Dr. James T. Jones, Jr/) and includes signatures made by electronic or mechanical means. S-signatures may be used in lieu of handwritten signatures for paper, facsimile, or EFS attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S-signature must consist only of letters and/or Arabic numerals with appropriate spaces and punctuation. A patent practitioner signing pursuant to §1.33(b)(1) or (2) must supply their registration number as part of or adjacent to the S-signature; the hash (#) may be used only before the registration number. Design practitioners must indicate 'design' adjacent to the last forward slash. The signer's name should be printed or typed preferably immediately below or adjacent to the S-signature and be reasonably specific so the identity can be readily recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic/graphic signatures for EFS submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system may be signed by a graphic representation of a handwritten signature or a graphic representation of an S-signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When electronically submitted via EFS, graphic representations of handwritten or S-signatures are acceptable as provided in paragraph (d)(1) and (d)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional electronic signatures as specified by Director
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence filed in the USPTO that requires a signature may be signed using an electronic signature personally entered by the signer and of a form specified by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent practitioner signing pursuant to §1.33(b)(1) or (2) must supply their registration number as part of the electronic signature or immediately adjacent. Design practitioners must indicate 'design' adjacent to the electronic signature. The signer's name should be printed/typed preferably immediately below or adjacent to the electronic signature and be reasonably specific to identify the signer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications on presentation of papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation to the Office (by signing, filing, submitting, or later advocating) of any paper by any party constitutes a certification under §11.18(b) of this subchapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations of §11.18(b)(2) may result in sanctions under §11.18(c); practitioners violating §11.18(b) may be subject to disciplinary action. The person inserting an S-signature or electronic signature certifies it is their own signature. A person submitting a document signed by another must have a reasonable basis to believe the signature was actually inserted by that person and should retain evidence of authenticity. Violations related to signature certification may result in sanctions under §11.18(c) and (d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and modification limits of USPTO forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office provides forms for public use to assist in filing correspondence and meeting requirements. Use of forms for purposes for which they were not designed is prohibited, and no changes to certification statements on Office forms may be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing text of a form (other than certification statements) may be modified, deleted, or added to only if all text identifying the form as an Office form is removed. Presentation of any Office form with text identifying it as an Office form constitutes a certification under §11.18(b) that the existing text and any certification statements on the form have not been altered other than as permitted by EFS-Web customization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may require ratification or evidence of authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require ratification, confirmation (which includes submission of a duplicate document with a proper signature), or other evidence of authenticity of a signature when the Office has reasonable doubt as to the signature's authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include variations of a signature or where the signature and the typed/printed name do not clearly identify the person signing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification required on correspondence about an application
rubrics_metrics.description: No correspondence relating to an application should be filed prior to receipt of the assigned application number. When correspondence concerns a previously filed application, it must identify conspicuously the application number (series code and serial number), or the serial number and filing date assigned by the USPTO, or the international application/registration number as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondence lacking such identification will be returned to the sender where a return address is available. If resubmitted within two weeks, original date of receipt will be considered under certain conditions (see §1.8/§1.10). In addition to application number, correspondence should state first listed inventor, title of the invention, filing date, and if known, the group art unit or examiner name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification required on correspondence about a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters concerning a patent (other than for maintenance fee payment) should state the patent number and date of issue, the name of the patentee, and the title of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For maintenance fee payments, see §1.366(c) for specific provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification for reexamination/supplemental examination correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: A letter relating to a reexamination or supplemental examination proceeding should identify the patent undergoing reexamination or supplemental examination by patent number, the request control number assigned to the proceeding, and, if known, the group art unit and name of the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identification aids proper routing and processing of reexamination-related correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application correspondence identification
rubrics_metrics.description: When a paper concerns a provisional application, it should identify the application as such and include the application number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps avoid confusion with non-provisional filings and preserves correct processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of receipt and Priority Mail Express date rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence received in the USPTO is stamped with the date of receipt, except that the Office is closed on Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays within the District of Columbia (except for facsimile or electronic filings as provided). Correspondence filed via Priority Mail Express (per §1.10) is stamped with the date of deposit as Priority Mail Express.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic filings via USPTO EFS receive a receipt date equal to the Eastern Time when the correspondence is received by the Office, regardless of weekends/holidays. Facsimile transmissions receive the date of complete transmission unless that date is a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday, in which case the next succeeding business day is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile transmission rules and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence (including authorizations to charge a deposit account) may generally be transmitted by facsimile; receipt date is the date the complete transmission is received, subject to weekend/holiday rules. Transmission sessions should be limited to correspondence for a single application or proceeding and must include the application/control/trial/interference/patent number as part of the sender's identification on the fax cover sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facsimile transmissions are NOT permitted and will not be accorded a date of receipt for certain items, including certified documents specified in §1.4(f), color drawings submitted under §§1.81–1.85 and other listed drawing sections, requests for reexamination (§1.510 or §1.913) or supplemental examination (§1.610), correspondence in an application subject to a secrecy order directly related to secrecy content, and contested cases and trials before the PTAB except as the Board may authorize. To facilitate processing, limit each session to a single application. See paragraph (d) for enumerated exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure if faxed continued prosecution (§1.53(d)) not evidenced as received
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office has no evidence of receipt of a continued prosecution application transmitted by facsimile under §1.53(d), the transmitting party may petition the Director to accord a filing date as of the transmission date if certain conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions include: (i) inform the Office promptly after learning no evidence of receipt exists; (ii) supply an additional copy of the previously transmitted application; (iii) include a statement attesting on personal knowledge (or to satisfaction of the Director) to the previous transmission and include a copy of the sending unit's report confirming transmission or other evidence that came into being after the transmission and within one business day. The Office may require additional evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure if EFS-submitted national stage correspondence not evidenced as received
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office has no evidence of receipt of national-stage correspondence submitted via USPTO EFS, the submitting party may petition the Director to accord the correspondence a receipt date as of the official submission date if certain requirements are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition requirements: (i) inform the Office promptly after learning no evidence of receipt exists; (ii) supply an additional copy of the previously submitted correspondence; (iii) include a statement attesting on personal knowledge (or to satisfaction of the Director) that the correspondence was previously officially submitted; (iv) supply a copy of an acknowledgment receipt generated by EFS or equivalent evidence confirming submission. The Office may require additional evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Times for taking action and expiration on weekends/holidays
rubrics_metrics.description: Periods specified in this part in days are calendar days. When the last day fixed for taking any action or paying any fee falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday within the District of Columbia, the action may be taken or fee paid on the next succeeding business day that is not a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the day that is twelve months after filing a provisional application falls on a weekend/holiday, the period of pendency is extended to the next succeeding business day not a weekend/holiday.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of mailing or transmission for timely filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence required to be filed within a set period will be considered timely filed if mailed/transmitted prior to expiration of the period and accompanied by a certificate stating the date of deposit or transmission, except in enumerated excluded situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The person signing the certificate should have a reasonable basis to expect the correspondence would be mailed/transmitted on or before the date indicated. The certificate procedure does NOT apply to specified items, including (relative to patents and patent applications): filing of a national patent application specification/drawing for obtaining a filing date (including a request for continued prosecution under §1.53(d)); papers filed in PTAB trials (governed by §42.6(b)); filing an international application for patent; filing correspondence in an international application before USRO/US ISA/US IPEA; filing a copy of the international application with basic national fee to enter national stage (§1.495(b)); filing a written declaration of abandonment under §1.138 (addressing requirements in §1.1(a)); filing a submission under §1.217 for publication of a redacted copy; filing a third-party submission under §1.290; calculation of any period of adjustment (§1.703(f)); filing an international design application; and disciplinary proceedings under part 11.

rubrics_metrics.name: If mailed/transmitted but not received, steps to preserve timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: If correspondence considered timely under the certificate procedure is not received after a reasonable time or the application is held abandoned or a proceeding dismissed/decided with prejudice, the correspondence may still be considered timely if the forwarding party: informs the Office promptly, supplies an additional copy and certificate, and includes a statement attesting on personal knowledge (or to satisfaction of the Director) of the previous mailing/transmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies also in contexts such as reexamination prosecution termination or requester paper refusal; further specific requirements and time limits are set out in the rules (see §1.8(b)).
